verdict_note: Based on reading only: no build and no tests were run. The core claims hold as built. There is no new Payload variant or NodeKind. Folio accepts exactly the four kinds sticky, shape_with_text, connector and section, and only with Payload::Vector, at the two kind-string sites (folio lib.rs:804 and :914). Any other payload falls through to PayloadMismatch, and the other eight kinds are still refused. The exporters (vector PDF, fig-native PDF, PSD loss) and composite dispatch on the payload, so they draw board nodes as vector paths, and the vector PDF draws the area text through prepare_vectors. There are 16 rows. A move with reroute and a delete are each one step, which swaps the layers and the whole vector entry, so undo and redo are exact for those two. A broken connector keeps its last route and reports connector_endpoint_node_unresolvable as a warning. The export is admitted through the shared JobPort helper. Two defects should be fixed before the bundled run. F1 (high): the layer delete row leaves a board record behind, and the vector tools mint ids without looking at the vector entry. So viewer.delete_layer on a sticky followed by viewer.draw_shape gives a 'vector' layer the sticky's id. After that, VectorEntry::decode fails with PayloadMismatch: every vector and board command and the canvas render fail, and the saved package carries the bad entry. F2 (high, partly declared): every text write mints a new story outside the history, and every redraw, move and reroute mints new path records. Nothing reclaims either one. A board therefore stops taking text after 256 text writes over its life (undone ones included), and stops taking all vector edits after 4096 path records. Neither limit is in the manual. F3-F6 (medium): undo names and record ids are not catalog ids (same class as DS-VARIABLES F3). `new --profile board` from the CLI writes a document that is not in whiteboard mode. A connector whose route collapses to one point makes its end nodes unmovable. Generic layer operations named by STU-WB-102 (pathfinder, outlines, arrange) drop board records or leave text behind without saying so. F7-F13 are low; F8 is the one visual defect: the ERD 'zero' ring draws as a solid dot. Visual capture: the PNG shows what the lane claims (section and label, square and wide stickies, rectangle, ellipse, diamond and cylinder with centred readable text, straight and elbowed connectors attached at the named sides, caps ARROW_EQUILATERAL, CIRCLE_FILLED, ERD_ONE, ERD_ZERO_OR_MORE and ARROW_LINES). No text overlaps. The one exception is F8.

findings.certainty: READ (mechanism); not run. The lane notes themselves state that the layer delete leaves the record ('a generic layer delete (layers.rs) ... leaves the record dormant'). The re-mint follows from mint_layer_id (lowest free id at or above the salt doc.layers.len()), which board_layer_id and create_vector_layer share. UNVERIFIED: whether Viewer::open then refuses the package or opens it without vector content.
findings.severity: high (an ordinary pair of drive rows makes the whole document's vector content unrenderable and every vector or board command refuse, and the saved package keeps the bad entry)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/layers.rs:51-62 (mint_layer_id), :188-245 (delete_layer: records_after_delete at :238-245 returns None for a document with no design records, crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/design/component.rs:816-822, so a board delete is a plain structure step that leaves board_nodes and area_texts); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/vector.rs:1896-1915 (create_vector_layer mints with plain mint_layer_id at :1900, no entry check; store_entry :1884-1893 validates nothing against the new layer), :2665-2711 (pathfinder, same), :1584-1609 (free_layer_ids checks area/path texts but not board_nodes); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/vector.rs:553 and :672-673 (VectorEntry::decode runs validate_records against the document); crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/board.rs:415-419 (a present layer whose kind differs from its record is PayloadMismatch); crates/hsk-studio-harness/src/cli/drive_viewer.rs:245 (delete_layer) and :390 (draw_shape) are drive rows
findings.what: Board records are keyed by layer id and live in the vector entry. The lane's own creates avoid ids that a board record still names (write.rs:87-106). The layer delete row keeps the record, and the vector tools' id minting ignores board records. Once a non-board layer takes a recorded id, validate_board_records refuses the whole record set. VectorEntry::decode then fails, which takes down vector_entry(), prepared_vectors (render), every vector and board edit, and board.read. Variant: duplicate_layer of another sticky can re-mint a deleted sticky's id. The copy (kind sticky) then silently adopts the old record and its old text binding.
findings.scenario: Board document (no layers). board.sticky.create {x:0,y:0,text:'A'} mints SLYR-...-7ede-9000-000000000000. viewer.delete_layer on it: layers empty, record and area text kept. viewer.draw_shape {kind: rectangle}: mint_layer_id(doc, 0) returns the same id with kind 'vector'. Next board.read or any vector command fails with vector_entry_vector_records: PayloadMismatch; the canvas refuses; document.save writes the entry.
findings.fix: (1) Extend records_after_delete (or a board twin called from delete_layer) to drop the deleted layers' board_nodes and their area_texts in the delete's own step. Connectors naming them then read broken, as designed, and undo brings the records back through the entry swap. Give duplicate_layer a decision too: copy the record under the new id, or declare. (2) Route every layer-id mint through one helper that avoids every id the vector and text entries name (free_layer_ids plus board_nodes), and use it in create_vector_layer, pathfinder and copy_subtree. (3) Lead question 1: should VectorEntry::decode report a record-kind mismatch as an issue instead of refusing the whole entry?
findings.test: tests/board.rs, new test a_layer_delete_then_a_drawn_shape_keeps_the_board_readable: sticky.create, viewer.delete_layer, viewer.draw_shape. Then assert board.read ok, a render ok, save and reopen ok, and no board_nodes record for the deleted id. Undo of the delete returns the record.

findings.certainty: READ; not run. The 256-story cap is declared in the lane notes (sibling_gaps). That it is a lifetime cap (undone and replaced stories count), and the path-record cap, are not declared.
findings.severity: high (a whiteboard stops taking any text after 256 text writes in its life, and stops taking any vector or board edit after 4096 path records; both hold after save and reopen; the manual names neither)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/board/write.rs:38-73 (board_story: a new story and two new styles per call; cap check :39-41), :131-134 (text entry written before and outside the step), :166 and :355-361 (every create and every set_text or section rename mints a story), :109-116 (board_path: a new SVPT per drawn path), :269-285, :313, :447-459 (redraw, reroute and move mint new paths; old ones stay); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/text.rs:44 and :88 (MAX_TEXT_LAYERS 256 on stories); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/vector.rs:61 (MAX_PATHS 4096) and :737-755 (to_bytes writes every path; no prune at save or decode); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/manual.rs:370-385 (DRIVE_LIMITS: neither cap)
findings.what: Stories: delete_node and undo never remove a story, and nothing prunes unbound stories, so the text entry only grows. With 100 stickies each edited once, the board is at 200 stories. The 257th text write anywhere in the document, including a plain text layer, refuses text_entry_over_budget, forever. Paths: the vector tools use the same new-path-per-edit scheme (arrange.rs:170-196), but a board makes it routine, because each move also redraws every attached connector. One node with 3 connectors moved 1000 times adds 4000 records, and then every board and vector edit refuses vector_entry_over_budget. Folio's MAX_BOARD_NODES 65,536 can never be reached.
findings.scenario: board.sticky.create once, then board.node.set_text on that sticky 300 times: call 256 refuses text_entry_over_budget, and so does every later board text command, also after save and reopen.
findings.fix: (1) After the rebase over SMB-DS-VARIABLES-AUTHOR-1 (it lands before this lane and adds the multi-entry step, harness.rs +82 lines), write the text entry inside the board step. Rewrite the node's own story in place under a stable id per node: undo then swaps the text back, and no orphan stays (this also closes F7). (2) At save, drop stories that no text layer, area text or path text names, and path records that no layer payload, live, network or record names. The history is not in the package (DRIVE_LIMITS line 2), so nothing can return to them. Do the same at open for older files. (3) State the remaining caps in DRIVE_LIMITS. Lead question 2.
findings.test: tests/board.rs: three_hundred_text_edits_keep_the_board_editable (300 set_text, then sticky.create ok, then stories in the text entry at most the live text nodes plus the history the step can return to); a_thousand_moves_keep_the_vector_entry_bounded (or: save and reopen gives a path count equal to the live paths); undo_and_redo_of_set_text_restore_the_text_entry_byte_for_byte.

findings.severity: medium (HOST INTEGRATION (3)-(5): records, history steps and undo names of every board edit name layer.* rows; same class as review F3 of SMB-DS-VARIABLES-AUTHOR-1)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/board/write.rs:121-137 (board_commit); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/harness.rs:1494-1497 and :1447-1462 (restructure_and_entry: command id 'layer.restructure_and_entry', label '{op} {first layer}'), :1315-1319 and :1383 with :329 (set_vector_paths_and_entry: 'layer.set_vector_paths_and_entry', label '{op} vector_paths'); crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/harness/containers.rs:342-344 (board.add records artboard.add, label add_artboard); crates/hsk-studio-harness/src/cli/drive.rs:302-309 (undo_name is the step label); tests/board.rs:461-464
findings.what: Take board.node.move. Its undo name is 'board_node_move vector_paths' and its step's command is layer.set_vector_paths_and_entry. board.sticky.create gives 'board_sticky_create SLYR-...' under layer.restructure_and_entry, and board.add gives artboard.add. None of these is the catalog id, so a host cannot map the step back to its RUN_COMMANDS row. The test checks only that undo_name is a string. Its attribution check reads reply.attribution, which drive builds from the Run context (drive.rs:125): it is the same for every reply, so it cannot fail.
findings.scenario: Over drive: board.node.move. Then reply.detail.undo_name == 'board_node_move vector_paths', and history.undo_steps[-1].command_id == 'layer.set_vector_paths_and_entry'.
findings.fix: Apply the fix the lead picks for DS-VARIABLES F3 here too: a command-id parameter on restructure_and_entry and set_vector_paths_and_entry (or a Run wrapper), with the row id as the command and 'catalog id + target' as the label. board.add passes board.add to container_edit. Lead question 3.
findings.test: In the_workshop_board_steps_run_through_the_jsonl_loop, assert undo_name == 'board.node.move <node>' (or the adopted form), assert history().undo_steps[-1] command_id and actor for each step, and drop the reply.attribution assertion.

findings.certainty: READ; not run (computed by hand from anchor, route, simplify and connector_drawing)

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-composite/src/board.rs:109-118 (AUTO), :131-159 and :162-178 (route and simplify collapse coincident ends to one point), :509-512 (connector_drawing refuses fewer than 2 points); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/board/write.rs:308-312 (reroute skips only connector_endpoint_node_unresolvable and returns any other error), :460-461 (move), :365-369 (resize by set_text or sticky.set)
findings.what: Suppose a node moves or grows so that both ends of an attached connector resolve to the same point. The reroute then refuses board_geometry_invalid, and so does the whole command. The node can be moved only after the connector is changed or deleted. board.read already has a state for this ('unroutable', board.rs:641-645), but the write path refuses instead of using it.
findings.scenario: Sticky A at (0,0), sticky B at (600,0) (both 240 by 240), connector AUTO to AUTO. board.node.move B to (240,0): both ends resolve to (240,120), the route is [(240,120)], and the move refuses board_geometry_invalid. Same when B moves onto A's place: equal centres pick RIGHT at both ends.
findings.fix: A connector that cannot be drawn after a move keeps its last drawing and route, and reads 'unroutable' (warning). The move goes ahead. Or draw a zero-length connector as its caps only. A self connector to the same magnet may keep its typed refusal at create. Lead question 5.
findings.test: tests/board.rs: moving_a_node_against_its_connected_neighbour_is_not_refused (the scenario above: move ok, connector state 'unroutable' or a drawn route, undo exact; then moving B away reroutes it to attached).

findings.what: A cancelled board export settles its job as failed('board_export_failed'), not canceled. The result does not carry the settlement, unlike settle_export_job. A board whose content is spread wide cannot be exported at any scale. The refusal is typed, but nothing in the manual says so.
findings.scenario: Cancel during the render: the job ledger says failed. Two stickies 1e6 apart: board.export_png refuses.
findings.fix: Use settle_export_job (or a text twin that maps 'canceled'), report job in the result, and add a scale or max-side parameter, or name the limit in the manual.
findings.test: A cancelled export settles canceled; an over-wide board refuses with a code the manual lists.

answers.payload_reuse_consumers: By reading, nothing breaks at the payload level. Exporters (vector PDF pdf_export.rs:287-290, fig-native export.rs:452-465, PSD doc_export.rs:742-750 as typed loss), composite and hit testing dispatch on Payload::Vector, so board nodes draw and export as vector paths; the vector PDF draws their area text. Kind-string sites: folio lib.rs:707 (initial_binding, board kinds pass), :804 and :914 (fixed), fig-base graph.rs:165 (import side, n/a). The V4-06 sites named not fixed are hosted.rs:1235, vector.rs:1526 and :2531. Semantic breaks come from operations that create, delete or replace layers without the board records (F1, F6), not from the kind strings.
answers.folio_kind_acceptance: Tight. Only the 4 bound kinds, only with Payload::Vector. Anything else falls to PayloadMismatch, and the other 8 kinds are still refused (unit test). The record-to-layer check (board.rs:415-419) is strict enough to make F1 fatal.
answers.older_readers: A board document cannot be read by builds before this lane. StudioVectorRecords is deny_unknown_fields (folio vector.rs:454), so boards and board_nodes are InvalidJson, and validate refuses kind 'sticky' as PayloadMismatch. Schema ids stay @1. This follows the precedent of earlier record members (lead question 7).
answers.undo_redo: Move with reroute: one set_vector_paths_and_entry step (layers' path ids plus the whole vector entry), so it is exact. Delete: one restructure_and_entry step, exact for layers and the vector entry; the connector records are untouched and come back attached. Not exact: the text entry, which is written outside the step (F7, F2). Undo names: F3.
answers.degenerate_connectors: Zero length (two equal positions) and the same node with the same magnet or AUTO on both ends: refused at create as board_geometry_invalid (typed). Self-reference to the connector itself: connector_endpoint_self. Connector to connector: not_attachable. The same node with different magnets (TOP to BOTTOM) draws a straight line through the node. Overlapping magnets of different connectors are fine. A route that later becomes degenerate blocks the move (F5).
answers.text_binding: board.* resizes rebind area_texts.container_id to the new outline and reset the first baseline (write.rs:269-285). A move rebinds per path (:453-455). A delete removes the binding in the step. Vector-tool transforms do not rebind (F6).
answers.persistence: boards and board_nodes ride the vector entry. The save and reopen test compares board.read nodes, and the JSONL test reopens 5 nodes. Not covered: a broken connector or dev_status through reopen (F11). Records left by the layer delete persist and can poison the entry (F1).
answers.caps: Folio caps (1000 boards, 65,536 node records, 64 route points, 256-byte author name) are charged before the walk. The binding limits are the 256-story text entry and the 4096 path records, both over the document's life (F2), and neither is in the manual.
answers.host_integration: Typed refusals: yes; codes come from 'board: <code> (...)' through engine_refusal, and helper errors are coded tokens. Attribution: commits run in the caller's Run context; author_name defaults to the actor's account id. One record per mutating command, but it names layer.* (F3). Reads emit one command_outcome frame. JobPort: admitted through the shared helper; cancel maps to failed (F13).
answers.visual: Readable text, no overlaps. Connectors are attached at the named or AUTO sides. Caps appear at both ends where set. The section frame and label are visible (label small and light grey, but readable). Defect: the ERD zero ring is solid (F8). The capture shows 5 of the 12 caps and 4 of the 12 native shapes, so it proves no more than that; the shapes test proves only that every native shape renders without a refusal.
